```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ranger)
 
# ===========================================================================
# Compare learnability of treatment-specific outcome surfaces
# for one study condition:
#   n_train = 1000
#   imbalance = 0.5
#   test location = stratified
#   treatment assignment = random
#   covariate omission = none
#
# For each replicate, fit random forests separately within observed
# control and treatment groups using df_train, then compare OOB performance.
# ===========================================================================
 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Pick one study condition and keep one training dataset per replicate.
#    Because results has one row per learner, distinct(run_id) avoids
#    counting the same replicate four times.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
one_condition <- results |>
  filter(
    n_train == 1000,
    prop_not_treated == 0.5,
    test_plot_location == "stratified",
    assignment == "random",
    var_omit == "none"
  ) |>
  distinct(run_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
 
# Check expected number of replicates; should be 50 if all reps are present.
one_condition |>
  summarise(
    n_replicates = n(),
    min_run_id   = min(run_id),
    max_run_id   = max(run_id)
  ) |>
  print()
 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define covariates and outcome.
#    Change covnames if your actual learner covariate set differs.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
covnames <- c(
  "soil_moist_code",
  "soil_carbon_initial",
  "no_of_stems",
  "mat_5yr",
  "map_5yr",
  "altitude"
)
 
outcome_var <- "soil_carbon_obs"
 
rf_formula <- as.formula(
  paste(outcome_var, "~", paste(covnames, collapse = " + "))
)
 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Function to fit separate random forests in control and treatment arms.
#    tr == 0: control
#    tr == 1: treatment
#    NOTE: do NOT add run_id inside this function, because run_id is already
#    outside the nested oob column.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
estimate_oob_by_arm <- function(dat) {
 
  dat |>
    mutate(
      arm = case_when(
        tr == 0 ~ "Control arm",
        tr == 1 ~ "Treatment arm",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      )
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(arm)) |>
    group_by(arm) |>
    group_modify(~ {
 
      fit <- ranger(
        formula   = rf_formula,
        data      = .x,
        num.trees = 500,
        seed      = 1
      )
 
      tibble(
        n_arm    = nrow(.x),
        oob_r2   = fit$r.squared,
        oob_rmse = sqrt(fit$prediction.error)
      )
    }) |>
    ungroup()
}
 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Apply across replicate training datasets.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
oob_by_arm <- one_condition |>
  select(run_id, df_train) |>
  mutate(
    oob = map(df_train, estimate_oob_by_arm)
  ) |>
  select(run_id, oob) |>
  unnest(oob) |>
  mutate(
    arm = factor(
      arm,
      levels = c("Control arm", "Treatment arm")
    )
  )
 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Summarise OOB performance by arm.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
oob_summary <- oob_by_arm |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(
    n_replicates  = n(),
    mean_n_arm    = mean(n_arm),
    sd_n_arm      = sd(n_arm),
    mean_oob_r2   = mean(oob_r2, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_oob_r2     = sd(oob_r2, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_oob_rmse = mean(oob_rmse, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_oob_rmse   = sd(oob_rmse, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
 
print(oob_summary)
 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot OOB R2.
#    Higher OOB R2 = easier outcome surface to learn.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
p_oob_r2 <- ggplot(oob_by_arm, aes(x = arm, y = oob_r2, colour = arm)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.45,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0),
    alpha = 0.75,
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Control arm"   = "#2C7FB8",
      "Treatment arm" = "#D6604D"
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression("Random forest OOB " * R^2),
    title = "Learnability of treatment-specific outcome surfaces",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "n = 1000, imbalance = 0.5, test = stratified, ",
      "assignment = random, no covariate omission"
    ),
    caption = paste0(
      "Each point is one replicated virtual study. ",
      "Random forests were fit separately within observed control and treatment arms. ",
      "Higher OOB R² indicates a more predictable outcome surface."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
 
p_oob_r2
 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Plot OOB RMSE.
#    Higher OOB RMSE = harder outcome surface to learn.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
p_oob_rmse <- ggplot(oob_by_arm, aes(x = arm, y = oob_rmse, colour = arm)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.45,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0),
    alpha = 0.75,
    size = 2
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Control arm"   = "#2C7FB8",
      "Treatment arm" = "#D6604D"
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Random forest OOB RMSE",
    title = "Learnability of treatment-specific outcome surfaces",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "n = 1000, imbalance = 0.5, test = stratified, ",
      "assignment = random, no covariate omission"
    ),
    caption = paste0(
      "Each point is one replicated virtual study. ",
      "Random forests were fit separately within observed control and treatment arms. ",
      "Higher OOB RMSE indicates a harder-to-learn outcome surface."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
 
p_oob_rmse
 
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Save plots.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 
ggsave(
  "arm_specific_oob_r2_n1000_balanced_stratified_random_no_omit.png",
  p_oob_r2,
  width = 6,
  height = 4.5,
  dpi = 300
)
 
ggsave(
  "arm_specific_oob_rmse_n1000_balanced_stratified_random_no_omit.png",
  p_oob_rmse,
  width = 6,
  height = 4.5,
  dpi = 300
)
```
